strings.Accesos PMR, plataformas hasta la orilla: Step-free routes, beach access platforms and how to check assisted bathing before your visit.
strings.Las Alcaravaneras dispone de itinerarios: Las Alcaravaneras has accessible routes from the promenade and priority areas for people with reduced mobility (PRM).
strings.La playa es extensa y las distancias sob: The beach is wide, and distances across the sand can be considerable. Use our
strings.para localizar los accesos PMR, el punto: to find accessible routes, the assisted-bathing point, toilets and showers.
strings.La disponibilidad de equipamiento y pers: Equipment and staff availability may vary with the season, sea conditions and ongoing works.
strings.El proyecto municipal contempla cuatro p: The municipal project includes four grooved, non-slip walkways across the sand to make it easier to reach the water. In 2026, plans were also announced for a shaded rest area prioritised for people with reduced mobility at the north access, along with ramps and seating improvements.
strings.Ciudad de Mar publica información del se: Ciudad de Mar provides information about assisted bathing and lists these contact numbers:
strings.. Llama antes de desplazarte para confir: . Call ahead to confirm whether the service is operating at Las Alcaravaneras, its hours, how to request it and what equipment is available.
strings.La información turística oficial enumera: Official tourism information lists accessible toilets and a priority area for people with reduced mobility. Ciudad de Mar says the bathing facility offers a service for visitors with reduced mobility and publishes daily hours of 11:00–18:00; check that these are still current before you go. The City Council has also announced upgrades to showers and foot-wash stations, so check which facilities are open.
strings.El vídeo muestra la instalación de una p: The video shows a 30-metre walkway installed to make reaching the sea more comfortable.
strings.El baño asistido y el socorrismo pueden: Assisted bathing and lifeguard cover may be seasonal. Ciudad de Mar publishes lifeguard periods and contact numbers for assisted bathing, but no specific hours for this support. Call before visiting to confirm availability, meeting point, whether you need to book and the conditions that day.

strings.Las Alcaravaneras: ¿de dónde viene el no: Las Alcaravaneras: where does our beach get its name?
strings.El nombre de la playa guarda una pista s: The beach's name holds a clue to the sandy expanses that once lay here and the bird that may have lived among them.
strings.Artículo histórico sobre el nombre de La: Historical article about the name Las Alcaravaneras
strings.Hoy conocemos Las Alcaravaneras como una: Today, we know Las Alcaravaneras as an urban beach surrounded by buildings, avenues and boats. It is a place to walk, swim, play sports or simply sit and look out to sea.
strings.Pero hace muchos años todo aquello era m: But many years ago, it all looked very different. Where we now see streets and buildings, there were wide stretches of sand and stony ground. One special name has survived from that landscape:
strings.¿De dónde viene ese nombre? Para encontr: Where does the name come from? To find a possible answer, we need to meet a small inhabitant of those old sandy expanses: the stone-curlew.
strings.Una playa que antes era mucho más grande: A beach that used to be much larger
strings.Hace más de cien años, el nombre de Alca: More than a hundred years ago, the name Alcaravaneras referred to more than the beach we know today. It was used for a much larger area of Santa Catalina, with sandy and stony ground.
strings.Aquellos espacios llegaban hasta lugares: Those open areas reached as far as places now known as Ciudad Jardín and Mesa y López. It is hard to picture, isn't it? The city was much smaller then, and the landscape was made up of open ground, dunes and paths.
strings.La playa actual formaba parte de una zon: Today's beach was part of a wider coastal area known as the Caleta de Santa Catalina. Over time, the city grew, the port changed, and new avenues and buildings were built. Much of that landscape gradually disappeared.
strings.Un nombre que viene de un ave: A name linked to a bird
strings.El alcaraván es un ave que vive en terre: The stone-curlew is a bird that lives in open, dry and stony places. It has large eyes and long legs. It can be easy to miss, but it is a fascinating bird.
strings.Según explica el investigador Humberto P: Researcher Humberto Pérez Hidalgo explains in his book
strings.Origen y noticias de lugares de Gran Can: Origins and stories of places in Gran Canaria
strings., el alcaraván vivía antiguamente en los: , the stone-curlew once lived in this area. Its presence could explain the name Alcaravaneras.
strings.No tenemos un documento antiguo que cuen: We do not have an old document that tells us exactly how the name began, so this is a likely explanation, not an absolute certainty. It fits the landscape that existed at the time.
strings.Un nombre que ya existía hace más de 180: A name already in use more than 180 years ago
strings.¿Y cómo sabemos que el nombre Alcaravane: How do we know that the name Alcaravaneras was used so long ago?
strings.En el Archivo Histórico Provincial de La: The Provincial Historical Archive of Las Palmas preserves a description of a municipal file from 1841–1842. It mentions land in Alcaravaneras, in Santa Catalina, as well as an irrigation channel: a small canal that carried water to fields.
strings.Esto demuestra que el nombre ya se utili: This shows that the name was already in use more than 180 years ago. It was probably known even earlier!
strings.Así eran los antiguos arenales: What the old sandy expanses looked like
strings.Las fotografías antiguas nos permiten vi: Old photographs let us travel back in time and imagine what this part of the city looked like before it filled with buildings and roads.
strings.Consultar la fotografía «Arenales en San: View the photograph “Arenales en Santa Catalina” in FEDAC's official record ↗
strings.Al observar la fotografía, podemos hacer: The photograph gives us an idea of just how much the landscape has changed.
strings.¿Quieres ver cómo es el alcaraván?: What does a stone-curlew look like?
strings.Este vídeo muestra alcaravanes en Lanzar: This video shows stone-curlews in Lanzarote. It was not filmed at our beach, but it helps us get to know the bird that may have inspired its name.
strings.El nombre de Alcaravaneras se utilizaba: In the past, the name Alcaravaneras was used for an area much larger than today's beach. The name has survived the city's growth and still reminds us what this place was like many years ago!
strings.Hoy, cuando caminamos por la playa, quiz: When we walk along the beach today, we may not think about the old sandy expanses or the birds that lived there. But its name preserves a small clue to a landscape that has almost disappeared.
strings.Archivo Histórico Provincial de Las Palm: Provincial Historical Archive of Las Palmas, inventory of the Las Palmas de Gran Canaria City Council collection. File from 1841–1842.
strings.Descubre cómo eran los antiguos arenales: Discover what the old sandy expanses of Santa Catalina looked like and which bird may explain the name Alcaravaneras.
